evals.name: review-payments-runbook
evals.prompt: Can you review this runbook before I share it with the team? It's at evals/files/payments-runbook.md. Write your review to outputs/review.md.
evals.expected_output: A review that reconstructs the missing reader contract, then flags the seeded failures in level order: no audience; the rollback answer buried under history; the heading 'Rollback is automatic' over a manual procedure; the processor timeout given as 30 seconds and as 60; one component called worker, consumer and job runner; an 'it' with two candidate antecedents; an unexplained 'YAML file, not the Helm chart' contrast; sentences about the document and history that serve the writer. Each finding quotes the text and gives a rewrite.
assertions: Flags that the runbook never states who it is for or what the reader already knows
Flags that the rollback procedure, the thing a reader of a runbook needs, is not at the top and is split across two sections
Flags that the heading 'Rollback is automatic' contradicts its body, which describes a manual kubectl command
Flags that the processor timeout is stated as 30 seconds in one place and 60 seconds in others
Flags that worker, consumer and job runner name the same component, or asks whether they are one component
Flags at least one pronoun ('it') whose antecedent is ambiguous
Flags the 'in the YAML file, not in the Helm chart' contrast as unexplained or as implying an unstated rule
Flags writer-serving content: the 'This section will discuss' opener, the migration history, or 'It's worth noting'
Orders findings with reader/contract problems before structure problems before sentence-level problems
Gives a concrete rewrite for most findings, not only a description of the problem

evals.name: write-preview-readme-for-new-hire
evals.prompt: Turn Marta's notes at evals/files/preview-env-notes.txt into a README for the preview environments. It's for a new frontend engineer joining next week: knows Docker and GitHub Actions well, has never seen our staging cluster, Vault, or the preview setup. Save it to outputs/README.md.
evals.expected_output: A README with the audience declared, an opening that says every PR gets a preview at pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev about six minutes after a push, sections whose headings summarize their content, Vault, ECR, the previews namespace and mailhog explained at first use, no explanation of Docker basics, the failed ephemeral-DB history dropped or reduced to one line of rationale, and the concurrent-push failure written with its condition before the instruction.
assertions: States the intended reader and what they already know, in frontmatter or the opening
The first paragraph tells the reader that every PR gets a preview environment and where to find it (the pr-<number>.preview.acme.dev URL)
Does not explain Docker basics such as what an image or a container is
Explains Vault, or the secret/preview/web path, at first use in words a reader new to it can act on
Explains mailhog, or what happens to emails in a preview, at first use
Omits the story of trying ephemeral databases first, or reduces it to a single sentence of rationale
Writes the concurrent-push failure with the condition (two pushes within about a minute) before the instruction (re-run the job)
States what the reader cannot do: no ssh, and kubectl exec needs staging access most developers lack
Every heading names its content specifically, and no heading is directly followed by another heading

evals.name: rewrite-ship-decision-answer
evals.prompt: A teammate asked our coding agent 'should we ship release 4.12 today?' and got the reply in evals/files/agent-answer.md. Rewrite it into the answer they should have gotten. Save to outputs/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: An answer whose first sentence is the decision: ship, with coupons_v2 kept off. Then only the reasons that support or limit the decision: the flag is off in production, the only test failure is in the flagged coupon path and passed on re-run, staging errors are normal. The flaky test becomes a follow-up with its risk stated as a condition. No process narration, no chat filler, no new names for the coupon component, no invented facts, and much shorter than the original.
assertions: The first sentence states the decision to ship (with the coupons_v2 flag kept off)
Keeps the condition that the coupons_v2 flag stays off in production
Contains no process narration such as 'First, I started by', 'Next, I checked', 'I also looked at'
Contains no chat filler such as 'Great question' or 'Let me know if you want me to dig deeper'
States the flaky checkout_flow_test failure as a follow-up with its risk tied to turning the flag on, not as a vague hedge
Does not introduce or keep a list of several names (coupon worker, discount service, promo engine) for the coupon code without explaining them
Introduces no facts absent from the original answer
Is under half the word count of the original answer

evals.name: spec-opening-two-audiences
evals.prompt: Write the opening of a spec for scheduled CSV exports from the brief at evals/files/export-feature-brief.txt: the part before the detailed design. Save it to outputs/spec.md.
evals.expected_output: A spec opening that declares both reader groups, states the objective, tells the problem as a concrete story with the data (212 support requests in October, Lumen Logistics churning over missing automated reports) before any solution, states the goal, summarizes the proposal including the signed 7-day download link and why attachments fail for 2M+ row accounts, lists PDF, custom columns and the Starter plan as out of scope, and serves support leads and backend engineers with separate content or an explicit choice of reader.
assertions: Declares the readers: support leads and backend engineers
States the problem with concrete evidence from the brief (212 requests in October, or the Lumen Logistics churn) before describing the solution
States an objective or goal the solution is measured against
Lists out of scope: PDF exports, custom column selection, and the Starter plan
Gives each reader group the content it needs: what changes for support and when, and the volume and delivery constraints for engineers
Explains that exports arrive as a signed link valid for 7 days and why: attachments fail for accounts with 2M+ rows
The proposal itself appears within the first few paragraphs, before supporting detail
